tasks.short: Set funeral prices and credit terms

steps.what: Check funeral products, service costs and candidate prices or credit terms
Calculate margins and payment schedules for specified funeral price scenarios
Set prices or credit terms after assessing affordability, costs and service obligations

tasks.design: Configure existing {SPREADSHEET} formulas or native {ERP} pricing scenarios for arithmetic. The manager establishes inputs, selects prices and credit policy, and approves the exact version before staff use it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual recalculation repeats when a candidate price or payment schedule changes.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit costs and proposed terms support ordinary formulas without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Fair pricing, affordability and appropriate credit terms require commercial and ethical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Balance service quality and financial sustainability sensitively.
tasks.altitude: Compare explicit options while retaining responsibility for the policy.

reach.learn: How to communicate monetary choices without pressuring vulnerable people

evidence.claim: Explicit prices, quantities, costs and payment dates support deterministic scenario arithmetic; local savings and policy suitability remain unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is setting general prices and credit policy, excluding individual credit assessment, customer agreement and payment collection. No automated credit eligibility decision is proposed.

Suppliers and accounting staff produce existing cost records before s1. The manager captures product/service IDs, quantities, cost amounts/currency, applicable tax treatment supplied by accounting, resource estimates, candidate prices and exact installment amounts/dates in s1; its 30 hours include checking and missing-data clarification. No free cost-ready or credit-approved flag exists; unsupported terms use manual calculation and review.
Test native pricing tables and protected spreadsheet formulas first. No other-role data cleanup is newly required; existing source production remains unchanged.
unknowns: Authority and local requirements for credit terms
research_questions: How much repeated calculation remains after native pricing functions and input verification are counted?

already_counted.description: Policy selection and exact version acceptance

approvals.approved_version: Exact products/services, price amounts, currency, effective date and credit terms recorded; changes require renewed manager approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B=100, R=80, gross=20, focal upkeep=5, net=15. Range 0-5 reflects infrequent policy changes, existing automatic formulas and substantial retained judgement.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review performance for service and cost opportunities

steps.what: Verify financial statements, sales reports and activity definitions for comparable periods
Compare financial and activity measures using explicit period and category mappings
Review comparisons to identify cost reductions or service improvements and investigate causes

tasks.design: Use native {ERP} exports and configured {SPREADSHEET} comparisons for compatible periods and categories. The manager checks the source definitions and interprets service consequences; a variance is a question rather than an automatic cost-cutting instruction.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated tabulation obscures the time available to investigate differences.
tasks.enabler_now: Fixed comparison definitions support deterministic aggregation and reconciliation.
tasks.still_hard: Changes in service mix, timing and care quality can explain apparent cost differences.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a useful improvement from a saving that damages the service.
tasks.altitude: Spend less time recalculating measures and retain contextual review.

reach.task: Investigate a cost variance against activity mix
reach.learn: How to distinguish volume effects from operational changes

evidence.claim: Verified period/category mappings support deterministic financial comparisons; this does not establish the cause of a variance or measured local savings.

assumptions: Boundary is manager review and opportunity identification, excluding source bookkeeping, execution of improvements and financial outcome claims.

Accounting and service staff produce their existing statements and activity records before s1 without new capture duties. In s1 the manager captures report versions, period boundaries, category mappings, amounts/currency, activity counts/units, exclusions and reconciliation totals, including manual transcription where needed. The 35 hours include all mapping and source checks. Missing definitions trigger manual review; no free normalized dataset or avoidable-cost flag is assumed.
Native reports and pivots precede custom code. Source collection shared with pricing is assigned once if the same episode serves both tasks.
unknowns: Report comparability and actual manual comparison share
Which quality measures accompany financial changes
research_questions: Does configured comparison reduce review effort after reconciliation and unmatched categories are included?

already_counted.description: Source capture, period/category mapping and reconciliation checks

incremental.description: Comparison definition maintenance and exception handling

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B=100, R=75, gross=25, focal upkeep=7, net=18. Range 0-8 allows existing automated reports, inconsistent service categories and extensive contextual investigation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Interview prospective employees and examine evidence against the role requirements
Decide whom to hire and communicate the authorized employment offer

tasks.design: Keep interview, evidence assessment and the hiring decision with the manager. Existing role and offer documents in {DOCS} support the work without automated ranking or an invented scheduling baseline.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sensitive funeral work requires assessment through direct discussion and relevant evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: No validated replacement for that assessment is established in the supplied evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Candidates need a fair opportunity to clarify experience and expectations.
tasks.human_edge: Assess role-relevant evidence without treating style or personal circumstances as a suitability score.
tasks.altitude: Interview and hiring time remain protected.

reach.learn: How to evaluate practical interpersonal requirements fairly

evidence.claim: The digest identifies hiring among sensitive employment uses; this design retains human interview and decision rather than proposing automatic ranking.
No local hiring-time saving follows from document access alone.

assumptions: Boundary is manager interview and hiring, excluding original vacancy creation, recruitment administration, payroll setup and candidate acceptance.

Candidates supply applications before s1 and responses during s1. Management or HR supplies authorized terms before the s2 offer; the manager checks and clarifies within retained time. Candidate acceptance arises after the offer outside this task; no ready-to-hire flag or acceptance is assumed.
Use existing documents and native recruitment facilities first. No new system or work transfer is proposed, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Manager hiring authority and employment terms approval arrangements
research_questions: Which interview activities establish the role-relevant evidence needed for a fair decision?

already_counted.description: Decision, terms verification and offer communication

approvals.approved_version: Exact candidate, role, employment terms and offer communicated; changed offer requires renewed manager acceptance within delegated authority.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Interview and accountable hiring remain full-time human work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Identify skill development needs through staff discussion and review of relevant work evidence

tasks.design: Retain manager judgement and staff discussion, using relevant existing evidence in {DOCS}. Do not infer individual skill gaps from complaint counts or an automatically generated performance score.
tasks.previous_blocker: A development need depends on task expectations, observed circumstances and the staff member's account.
tasks.enabler_now: No separate repetitive compilation share or reliable automatic gap judgement is established.
tasks.still_hard: A process problem can look like an individual skill problem.
tasks.human_edge: Discuss weaknesses constructively and distinguish learning support from blame.
tasks.altitude: Development assessment retains its full time.

reach.task: Discuss a service skill development need
reach.learn: How to distinguish individual learning needs from service process constraints

evidence.claim: Identifying a skill gap requires contextual evidence and staff discussion; no measured local time saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary is identifying development needs, excluding course delivery, certification and disciplinary decisions.

The manager supplies observations and role expectations; staff provide perspectives during s1 before the assessment closes. Evidence capture and clarification remain within retained time; no free competency score or verified-deficit flag is assumed.
Existing documents and native learning records come first. No new monitoring tool, delegated data entry or added upkeep is proposed.
unknowns: Actual training requirements and available observational evidence
research_questions: Which apparent skill gaps are better explained by unclear procedures or inadequate resources?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Human assessment retains its time without inventing a report-generation baseline.
